newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ice hockey-MAPLE LEAFS BEAT BLUES FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-MAPLE LEAFS BEAT BLUES FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Mike Craig had a goal and two assists and linemates Todd Warriner and Jamie Baker each added a goal and an assist as the Toronto Maple Leafs won their third straight, 6-3 over the St Louis Blues on Tuesday.
Sergei Berezin, Wendel Clark and Mats Sundin scored the other goals for Toronto, which has won six of its last seven games and avenged a 6-1 loss at St Louis.
"The way we started out, we lost five in a row, started at the bottom of the conference. And to put together three wins is huge," Craig said.

Warriner and Berezin scored 49 seconds apart early in the first period to put the Maple Leafs ahead to stay, 2-1. Warriner was credited with his first goal since last March 27 when his centering attempt from behind the net deflected in off goaltender Grant Fuhr's right skate.

Berezin snapped a shot from the slot into the top left corner for a power-play goal at 4:22 to break the tie. The Russian rookie has scored goals in three straight games. Sundin assisted on the tally and extended his point-scoring streak to seven games.
Craig's power-play goal with 32 seconds left in the opening period extended Toronto's lead to 3-1 and Baker made it a three-goal cushion at 7:45 of the second.
"We were telling ourselves things eventually have got to happen," Baker said. "Tonight, we were rewarded for hard work. It's definitely good for our line and our confidence."
Fuhr was replaced by Jon Casey after allowing four goals on only 10 shots. He returned late in the third period and finished with only seven saves.

St Louis, which has lost five of six, rallied in the second half of the second period. Stephane Matteau deflected rookie Jamal Mayers' shot past goalie Felix Potvin for a power-play goal at 13:07 and Harry York beat Potvin to a rebound to add a shorthanded tally that cut the margin to 4-3 with just four seconds to go in the period.
"Everything went downhill in the first," York said. "We salvaged it, but too late. We have to start a little earlier."

Doug Gilmour picked up assists on third-period goals by Clark and Sundin to seal the victory. Gilmour's first assist was the 700th of his career, making him the 29th player in NHL history to reach that plateau.
"It's an accomplishment, but right now, it's a team game and without my teammates I wouldn't have accomplished this," he said.
Sundin's goal was his 10th, moving him into a tie for the league lead.
Igor Kravchuk had the other goal for the Blues.
